requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1
requirements.summary: PV/VG/LV created (srv_data_vg/data_lv), formatted xfs, and mounted at /srv/data; test file written and checksummed to confirm usability.

requirements.requirement: Grow the LV to at least 2GB while it stays mounted and contents stay intact
requirements.summary: vgextend + lvextend to <2.15 GiB and xfs_growfs performed with /srv/data still mounted (no unmount/remount in the sequence); df confirms 2.1G filesystem; sha256sum of testfile.txt matches pre-growth value and file content is readable, confirming data integrity.

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) Provider-wide node-restart evidence: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (c2ffc729...) and healthy mount/service state captured, systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged (stream closed as node went down), post-restart polling confirmed exec availability, and post-restart state shows a new boot_id (0dd7a1f7...), srv-data-loop.service active, /srv/data auto-mounted at 2.1G via fstab, and testfile.txt checksum unchanged. Corroborated by fixed lifecycle snapshots (before_prepare boot-identity c2ffc729... vs after_executor boot-identity 0dd7a1f7...).

overall_summary: The executor satisfied both material task outcomes: an LVM logical volume was created and mounted at /srv/data, and it was grown live to over 2GB while remaining mounted with verified-intact contents (checksum match before and after growth). Because the node's single disk had no free space, the executor used loop-device-backed PVs and additionally engineered a systemd unit plus fstab entry so the setup survives a reboot; this went beyond the literal task wording but is a reasonable and well-justified implementation choice given the constraint, not a requirement violation. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, post-restart boot-identity change, and recovered mount/service/data state, cross-validated against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots.
limitations: Growth-while-mounted claim relies on the absence of any unmount command in the single combined shell invocation (cmd-bb68db024a854615) rather than a continuous mount-status trace spanning the entire operation.

The reboot-simulation mutation (cmd-23630ecb7b244c90) and its restoration were only observed through executor-issued commands, not an independent snapshot immediately before and after that specific action.

operational_hygiene.summary: One bounded, low-risk mutation outside the direct task/verification path was observed: cmd-23630ecb7b244c90 unmounted /srv/data, deactivated the VG, and detached both loop devices to manually simulate a boot cycle and validate the new systemd unit before performing a real reboot. This is a reasonable prerequisite check for a persistence mechanism that has no native udev/disk auto-discovery path, and it was fully restored within two subsequent commands (cmd-1f1e6da1ee174c35 re-started the service and re-activated the VG; cmd-52f54876a28447e1 remounted /srv/data and re-verified the checksum), leaving no residue. A temporary /tmp/reboot.log created by the backgrounded reboot command was cleaned up afterward (cmd-30729d0a613b4338). No abandoned files, failed/conflicting services, weakened security controls, or unexplained package-state changes are present in the after_executor snapshot versus after_prepare (failed-services empty in both, package-health unchanged, only expected boot-id/tmp/socket-PID changes from the reboot itself).
